title: Let Your Agent Cook: Using Skills to Evaluate and Improve Your App — Ankur Duggal, Arize AI
talk_summary: Speaker demos using CLI-backed skills to give a coding agent access to traces, evals, annotations, APM, and codebase so it can diagnose agent failures, build datasets/evals, and run experiments. The core loop is production trace -> failure dataset -> eval/experiment -> fix -> monitor, with sampling and human verification to control cost and avoid bad fixes.

takeaways.what_they_do: Expose production agent traces, existing evals, annotations, APM logs, and codebase to a coding agent; have it identify failure modes, build datasets, and run experiments against baseline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use this skill and pull down the traces from that specific agent. Find out what issues exist
takeaways.numbers: 44% bad summaries; 0% baseline to ~90% success after iterations

takeaways.what_they_do: Package platform actions as CLI/API skills so coding agents can query traces, datasets, evals, annotations, and trigger experiments without manual UI work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you give it access to these skills, what you're actually giving it access to is the CLI underneath

takeaways.what_they_do: Run LLM-as-judge evals on sampled traces/calls rather than 100%, and track eval cost per run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sample specific amounts so we don't run it across 100% of our traces and 100% of our calls

takeaways.what_they_do: Use trace evidence to keep agent focused on actual failure, then human verifies the fix improves the agent rather than just linting/degrading.
takeaways.evidence_quote: be the manual human to make sure that hey, it didn't just go back and fix the linting changes

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep evals running after prompt/skill changes to catch model regressions and shifted user questions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: two months later because there's a model regression because people start asking questions in a different way

takeaways.what_they_do: Create a dataset from failing production spans, run baseline and candidate fixes as experiments, and compare pass rates before shipping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the baseline, which was buggy, which as we expected would result in 0% uh passing rate
